newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia's PM candidate awaits approval for govt.
newsitem.headline: Estonia's PM candidate awaits approval for govt.

text.p: Estonia's prime ministerial candidate Mart Siimann presented his proposed government to the president on Friday but was still awaiting his approval, a spokesman for the president's office said.
"The president has not yet announced his decision," spokesman Ando Noormets told Reuters.
Under the Estonian Constitution, President Lennart Meri has three days to make a decision on the appointment of a prime minister and his proposed government once the line-up is presented.
Siimann was given the authority by parliament on Wednesday to form a new government and had to present his proposed government to the president within seven days.
Siimann, 50, will replace veteran politician Tiit Vaehi who stepped down last month after 22 months in office.
Vaehi's resignation came after he only narrowly won a no confidence motion in parliament amid allegations he was involved in shady privatisation deals involving real estate.
Siimann, a former television and radio station manager, is the parliamentary leader of the Coalition Party, one of the two largest groups in parliament.
No major changes are expected to the cabinet but the Education Minister Rein Loik has resigned for personal reasons and the position of Agriculture Minister is in some doubt.

Siimann has already assured the country that his government -- the seventh since Estonia regained independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991 -- would continue the previous government's economic policies and reforms.
"The new government sees its mission in continuing the reforms," Siimann told parliament on Wednesday.
